**What I found** (API 35 emulator; playground app built with `--split-per-abi -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true`; no `versionCode` in `android {}` or the manifest):
- **Fresh install works:** `adb uninstall`, then `adb install app-arm64-v8a-release.apk`, gives `Success`. `dumpsys package` shows `versionCode=0`.
- **Install over a `versionCode=7` build fails:** `adb install -r` gives `Failure [INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE]`.
- **Why:** with the flag, `configureSplitPerAbiVersionCodes` returns early. So every split APK keeps the same `versionCode`, which is 0 when none is set.

So "Android refuses to install" was wrong, and `@mboetger` is right. The flag doesn't help because the split APKs end up sharing one `versionCode`. Play rejects that, and Android refuses it as a downgrade over any build with a higher `versionCode`.

**Diff:**
```diff
--- a/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/ManifestVersionCodeTaskHelper.kt
+++ b/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/ManifestVersionCodeTaskHelper.kt
@@ -145,9 +145,12 @@
     /**
      * Formats the `--split-per-abi` error for [variantName] when `android {}` omits `versionCode`
      * and reading the main manifest fails ([reason]).
      *
-     * Does not suggest `force-version-code-ignoring-abi`, because it cannot help here. When the
-     * manifest has no positive `versionCode`, the flag builds APKs with no `versionCode`, which
-     * Android refuses to install. When the value is not a decimal integer, AGP fails the build.
+     * Does not suggest `force-version-code-ignoring-abi`, because it does not give the split APKs
+     * distinct `versionCode`s. When the manifest sets no `versionCode`, the flag builds every
+     * split APK with `versionCode` 0. Google Play rejects split APKs that share a `versionCode`.
+     * Android installs such an APK only where no build with a higher `versionCode` is installed;
+     * otherwise it fails with `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE`. When the value is not a decimal
+     * integer, AGP fails the build.
      */
```
